newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners still eschew costly foreign crudes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners still eschew costly foreign crudes.

text.p: U.S. refiners continued to eschew foreign crudes Tuesday in favor less expensive domestic grades amid moderate Latin American spot activity.
The spread between January West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent was at $1.10-15 a barrel, flat with late Monday.
"Brents are on offer, but they're still rather pricey," one trader said. "They're on offer at Jan WTI plus 35 cents, and would have to be 15-20 cents cheaper to get interest."
In Latin America, Argentine YPF sold a cargo of Medanito crude to Brazilian state oil company Petrobras for late December, trade sources said.
The cargo of 380,000 barrels was sold at less than January West Texas Intermediate minus $1.35 a barrel fob, the price at which it was last sold, traders said.
The cargo is to be delivered December 29-30.
Elsewhere, British Petroleum is offering a Cusiana cargo for late December, asking around February WTI plus 50-59 cents, traders said.
Colombian state Ecopetrol is offering a separate Cusiana cargo for January.

In the U.S. aftermarket, four partial January Brent cargoes changed hands among Wall Street traders at $23.80, $23.85 twice, and $23.86 a barrel, five to 11 cents higher than the IPE settlement price.
Intermonth spreads were steady with the London close. Brent Jan/Feb was done at 66 cents.
